narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Calm Tool Wall"**

Every tool is in view at once, sorted onto one wall by what it works on, and the page stays quiet while you look. The wall keeps its structure from the first version (five zones, one place per tool, every tool a white tag) but drops everything that shouted. The ground is a soft off-white, zones are pale washes of their colour with one small solid dot by the name, tags are plain white cards with a hairline edge, and the only type is the device's own face in sentence case.

The reason is the user's: the bright, saturated version felt stressful. That is the governing principle of this system. Colour is a quiet signpost, not the main event. It tells you where a tool lives at a glance and then gets out of the way; ink, white and generous space do the rest.

Tool pages carry the same calm: a breadcrumb back to the wall with the zone's dot and name, the tool's icon on a small tile of its zone's wash, and the tool itself on a bench, a 5% mat with a hairline border that says what goes in and what comes out before anything runs. Below sit How it works, Questions, and Related tools as the same white tags.
keyCharacteristics: Off-white ground on every wall page and tool page; white for tags, fields and the bench's inner surfaces.
Five zone colours used only as pale washes (5 to 12%) and 10px solid dots.
White tags with a 1px hairline border; hover turns the border ink and underlines the name.
System UI face only, sentence case everywhere, weight and size carry hierarchy.
Gently rounded: 8px on controls and tags, 16px on zones, tiles and benches.
Flat: no shadows, no gradients, no ornament. Motion is a 120ms colour or border change.
Ink controls (buttons, links, focus) at about 17:1 on the ground; every pair checked for WCAG AA.

rules.name: The Quiet Signpost Rule
rules.body: Colour says where a tool lives and is never the main event. A zone colour appears at full strength only as a 10px dot; every surface it touches is a wash of 16% or less. If a new surface makes colour the first thing you see, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink Controls Rule
rules.body: Buttons, links, focus rings and icons are ink. A zone colour never becomes a button, a link, a border or a focus ring.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: A developer tool is amber on every wall and every page. Group identity comes from the zone's name, never from a second colour.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every heading, label and button is sentence case. Nothing is set in uppercase or letter-spaced capitals.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Headings and text share the system face; hierarchy comes from weight (800, 700, 650, 600) and size. Mono is for what a visitor pastes or copies, never for labels.

rules.name: The walls
rules.body: On phones zones stack full width (8px side padding) and tags sit two to a row. From 720px the homepage wall is a six-column grid: Image, PDF and AI two columns each on top, Video two and Developer four below. The /developer/ wall is two columns from 720px and three from 1100px. Inside a zone, tags auto-fill at a 9.5rem minimum. The wall head is the headline over its subhead, 32px above the wall.

rules.name: The header
rules.body: One line: the wordmark left, "Your files never leave your device" in small muted text right, wrapping on narrow screens. The footer is one muted line over a hairline.

rules.name: The Every Tool Is In View Rule
rules.body: A wall shows every tool it holds at once; there is no carousel, tab or "show more" on a wall.

rules.name: The Hairline Lift Rule
rules.body: A tag shows it is live by its border turning from hairline to ink and its name underlining, over 120ms. Nothing moves, lifts or casts a shadow. Under reduced motion the change is instant.

dos: Do put every tool in exactly one zone and show it as a white tag.
Do keep zone colour to washes (16% or less) and the 10px dot, and keep every control ink.
Do show In → Out on every tool's bench before the tool runs.
Do give every tool page the breadcrumb, the icon tile on its zone's wash, and the bench.
Do use 8px corners on controls and tags, 16px on zones, tiles and benches.
Do write plain copy in sentence case ("Your files never leave your device").
Do draw icons as inline Lucide SVG at 1.8 stroke in ink, and status marks as drawn SVG masks.
Do keep tap targets at 44px or more and check every new colour pair for WCAG AA.
donts: Don't fill a surface with a saturated zone colour; the bright version was rejected as stressful.
Don't give a developer group its own colour; every developer tool is amber.
Don't add a display or web font, uppercase labels, tape labels or stamped codes.
Don't add drop shadows, glows, gradients, background patterns or decorative motion; a tag never moves.
Don't colour a button, link, border or focus ring with a zone colour.
Don't use text glyphs (↑ ↓ ✕ ⚠) for icons; draw them.
